mainTopic: The value of constant Torah study, מנשה's mockery of the Torah, the power of learning and teaching Torah, and who counts as an אפיקורוס
overview: The amud opens by stressing that Torah must be reviewed every day, like a song, and רבי אלעזר proves step by step that people were created for the toil of Torah. ריש לקיש warns against learning only on and off. A ברייתא then describes מנשה בן חזקיה, who mocked פסוקים that seemed pointless. A בת קול rebukes him, and the גמרא shows that those very פסוקים, about תמנע and about ראובן's דודאים, teach real lessons. Next come sayings on the power of Torah: learning it brings peace, builds and protects the world, and brings the גאולה closer. Teaching another person's child, or causing someone else to do a מצוה, is counted as if you did it yourself. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה's אפיקורוס and debates whether it means disgracing a תלמיד חכם or disgracing someone in front of one. It gives two versions of that argument and several examples. רבא's example, the family of בנימין the doctor, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Sing your learning every day
steps.stepSummary: The teaching that one must review Torah daily, like a song.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sing every day, sing every day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a teaching that started just before: review your Torah every day, the way people keep singing a favorite song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not one-time learning but steady repetition. The words are said twice to stress that this has to happen over and over.

keyTerms.meaning: Sing; here it means review your learning like a song

phrases.english: Sing every day,
phrases.notes: He means: go over your learning again and again, the way you would hum a song.

phrases.english: sing every day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the teaching from the previous section about constant Torah review.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah must be reviewed every day, like a song sung repeatedly.

steps.title: Asking for the source in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבודימי asks which פסוק teaches daily review.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר אבודימי said: What is the פסוק that teaches this?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בר אבודימי asks for a פסוק behind the idea of daily review. This sets up the next step, where he gives the answer himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא likes to anchor even ethical teachings in a פסוק. The question only prepares the ground; the answer comes next.

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Avudimi said:
What is the verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source of step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק supports the teaching of daily review?

steps.title: Work at Torah here, and it works for you there
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'נפש עמל עמלה לו' shows that effort in Torah here is repaid in another place.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'The soul of the worker works for him, because his mouth presses on him.' He works in this place, and his Torah works for him in another place.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק answers with a פסוק from משלי and explains it: the person works hard at Torah in this world, and his Torah 'works' for him in the next world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עמל appears twice in the פסוק, so it is read as two kinds of work: the person's work now and the Torah's work for him later. 'His mouth presses on him' points to learning out loud again and again, which fits daily review.

keyTerms.meaning: His mouth presses on him (he wears out his mouth with learning)
Another place, meaning the next world

phrases.english: As it is stated: 'The soul of the laborer labors for him,'
phrases.notes: משלי 16:26

phrases.english: 'for his mouth presses upon him.'
He labors in this place,
phrases.notes: 'This place' is this world.

phrases.english: and his Torah labors for him in another place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משלי 16:26: a person's work at Torah in this world is repaid by his Torah in the next world.

steps.title: Every person was created for effort
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that every person was created for עמל, based on a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Every person was created for effort, as it says: 'For man is born for toil.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר states a general idea: people were created to work hard. This opens a short step-by-step proof about what kind of effort is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in איוב only says 'toil' without saying what kind. The next steps will narrow that down.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Every person was created for toil,
as it is stated: 'For man is born for toil.'
phrases.notes: איוב 5:7

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל אָדָם לְעָמָל נִבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the same theme of עמל in Torah from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every person was created for toil.

steps.title: Toil of the mouth or physical work?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks whether 'toil' means speaking or physical labor.
steps.simpleTranslation: I don't know whether he was created for the toil of the mouth or for the toil of physical work.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר points out that the פסוק is unclear. Is the effort about using your mouth, or working with your hands? This sets up the next proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first of two narrowing questions. It splits 'toil' into two possible kinds.

phrases.aramaic: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם לַעֲמַל פֶּה נִבְרָא
phrases.english: I do not know whether he was created for toil of the mouth
or whether he was created for toil of labor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם לַעֲמַל פֶּה נִבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what kind of toil step 4 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the toil of the mouth or of physical work?

steps.title: It is toil of the mouth
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'כי אכף עליו פיהו' shows the toil is of the mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says 'for his mouth presses on him,' you must say he was created for toil of the mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר uses the same פסוק from משלי that appeared earlier to answer: the effort is with the mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'his mouth' in the פסוק settle the question. Physical labor is ruled out as the main purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say, so it must mean

phrases.english: When it says: 'For his mouth presses upon him,'
phrases.notes: The same פסוק from step 3, משלי 16:26.

phrases.english: you must say that he was created for toil of the mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר כִּי אָכַף עָלָיו פִּיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The toil is of the mouth, as the פסוק says 'his mouth presses upon him.'

steps.title: Torah or ordinary talk?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks whether mouth-toil means Torah or plain conversation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still I don't know whether it means the toil of Torah or the toil of conversation.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know it's the mouth, רבי אלעזר narrows further: talking Torah, or just talking? This sets up the final proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the second narrowing question. 'Mouth' could still mean any speech, so another פסוק is needed.

phrases.english: And still I do not know

phrases.aramaic: אִם לַעֲמַל תּוֹרָה אִם לַעֲמַל שִׂיחָה.
phrases.english: whether it is for the toil of Torah or for the toil of conversation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the answer of step 6 further.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the mouth-toil for Torah or for conversation?

steps.title: It is the toil of Torah
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'לא ימוש ספר התורה הזה מפיך' proves the toil is Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says 'This Torah scroll shall not leave your mouth,' you must say he was created for the toil of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings a פסוק from יהושע that ties the mouth to Torah, so the effort a person was made for is Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק connects 'your mouth' directly to Torah. That finishes the narrowing: toil, then toil of the mouth, then toil of Torah.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's three-step proof: people were created for toil (איוב), toil of the mouth (משלי), and specifically toil of Torah (יהושע).

phrases.english: When it says:
'This Torah scroll shall not depart from your mouth,'
phrases.notes: יהושע 1:8

phrases.english: you must say that he was created for the toil of Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר לֹא יָמוּשׁ סֵפֶר הַתּוֹרָה הַזֶּה מִפִּיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 and completes רבי אלעזר's proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The toil is of Torah, from יהושע 1:8.

steps.title: Bodies are containers, and lucky is the one who holds Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבא's saying matches רבי אלעזר: all bodies are containers, and fortunate is one who is a container of Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that is what רבא said: All bodies are containers. Fortunate is the one who merits to be a container for Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבא's well-known saying fits what רבי אלעזר just proved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every body holds something, like a storage vessel. The point is to fill it with Torah, which matches the idea that people were created for the toil of Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Fortunate is the one who merits

phrases.english: And this is what Rava said:
All bodies are containers.
phrases.notes: Like a storage bag that holds things until they're needed.

phrases.english: Fortunate is the one who merits
to be a container of Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links רבא's saying to the conclusion of step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Every person is a container; the ideal is to be filled with Torah.

steps.title: Learning on and off is like adultery
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads 'נואף אשה חסר לב' as referring to one who learns Torah only now and then.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who commits adultery with a woman lacks sense.' ריש לקיש said: This is someone who learns Torah only at intervals, as it says: 'It is pleasant if you keep them inside you; let them be ready together on your lips.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש reads a פסוק about adultery as a lesson about Torah: someone who learns only every so often 'lacks sense.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Torah should be kept inside you all the time and ready on your lips, as the second פסוק says. Learning only on and off breaks that steady connection, which is why it is compared to an unfaithful relationship.

phrases.english: 'One who commits adultery with a woman lacks understanding.'
phrases.notes: משלי 6:32

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
This is one who learns Torah at intervals,
as it is stated: 'For it is pleasant if you keep them within you;'
phrases.notes: משלי 22:18. 'Them' means the words of Torah.

phrases.english: 'let them be established together on your lips.'

steps.triggerLanguage: נֹאֵף אִשָּׁה חֲסַר לֵב. אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching on the theme of constant Torah study.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who learns Torah only on and off is called 'lacking sense'; Torah must be kept within constantly.

steps.title: The one who sins 'with a high hand' is מנשה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'והנפש אשר תעשה ביד רמה' as referring to מנשה בן חזקיה, who mocked the Torah's stories.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: 'And the person who acts with a high hand' — this is מנשה son of חזקיה, who would sit and give mocking interpretations of the Torah's stories.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא, linking a פסוק about brazen sinning to king מנשה. This opens a new section that will describe his mocking explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'With a high hand' means sinning openly and defiantly. The ברייתא gives מנשה as the example, because he publicly twisted the Torah's stories to make them look foolish.

keyTerms.meaning: Stories and narrative parts of the Torah

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
'And the person who acts high-handedly'
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:30

phrases.english: this is Manasseh son of Hezekiah,
who would sit and expound
stories in a mocking way.
phrases.notes: He would make fun of the Torah's stories, as the next lines will show.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה בְּיָד רָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new ברייתא, moving from Torah study to one who mocks the Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'high-handed' sinner of במדבר 15:30 is מנשה בן חזקיה, who mocked the Torah's stories.

steps.title: מנשה mocks seemingly pointless פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: מנשה asks scornfully why משה needed to write trivial-seeming פסוקים about תמנע and about ראובן finding flowers.
steps.simpleTranslation: מנשה said: Did משה have nothing better to write than 'And לוטן's sister was תמנע,' 'And תמנע was a concubine to אליפז,' and 'ראובן went in the days of the wheat harvest and found דודאים in the field'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now shows exactly how מנשה mocked the Torah. He picked out פסוקים that look like unimportant details and made fun of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said מנשה mocked the Torah's stories. Here we hear his actual words. His claim is that these פסוקים teach nothing, as if משה wrote them on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he have nothing else? (a mocking question)
A kind of plant or flower that ראובן found

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: וְכִי לֹא הָיָה לוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה
phrases.english: He said: Did Moshe have nothing
phrases.notes: "He" is מנשה from the previous step.

phrases.english: to write except "And Lotan's sister was Timna"
phrases.notes: בראשית 36:22

phrases.english: "And Timna was a concubine to Eliphaz"
phrases.notes: בראשית 36:12

phrases.english: "And Reuven went in the days of the wheat harvest
and found dudaim in the field"?
phrases.notes: בראשית 30:14

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: וְכִי לֹא הָיָה לוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה לִכְתּוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual words of the mockery mentioned in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנשה claimed that certain Torah פסוקים are pointless details written by משה.

steps.title: A heavenly voice rebukes מנשה
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול answers מנשה with פסוקים from תהלים, rebuking him for slandering the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בת קול came out and said to him: 'You sit and speak against your brother, you slander your mother's son. You did these things and I stayed silent; you thought I was like you. I will rebuke you and lay it out before your eyes.'
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven answers מנשה's mockery with a rebuke. Heaven tells him that God's silence does not mean He agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בת קול rejects מנשה's claim that these פסוקים are empty. He treated God's words as if a human wrote them, the way a person might be talked about behind his back. God now says He will show him the truth.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said to him:
"You sit and speak against your brother
you slander your own mother's son.
These things you did, and I kept silent;
you imagined that I was just like you.
I will rebuke you and lay it out before your eyes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the mockery from step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: מנשה's whole claim that these פסוקים are meaningless.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He treated God's Torah as human writing and took God's silence for agreement.

steps.title: A פסוק in ישעיהו describes מנשה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a פסוק in נביאים is about מנשה: people who drag sin with thin cords and then with a cart rope.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about him it says clearly in נביאים: 'Woe to those who drag sin with cords of falsehood, and sin like a cart rope.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא connects a פסוק from ישעיהו to מנשה. This sets up the next question about what the 'cart rope' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two images: thin cords and a thick cart rope. It hints that sin grows. The גמרא will explain this image next.

phrases.english: And about him it is stated clearly in the tradition:
phrases.notes: "The tradition" here means the books of the נביאים.

phrases.english: "Woe to those who drag sin with cords of falsehood
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 5:18

phrases.english: and sin as with a cart rope."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a פסוק from נביאים that describes מנשה's sin.

steps.title: What does 'like a cart rope' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the image of a cart rope means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'like a cart rope' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the cart-rope image. This sets up רבי אסי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about one specific phrase in the פסוק. The גמרא wants to know why sin is compared to a thick rope.

phrases.english: What is "as with a cart rope"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the פסוק from step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the cart-rope image.

steps.title: רבי אסי: the יצר הרע grows from thread to rope
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי explains that the יצר הרע starts thin like a spinning thread and ends up thick like a cart rope.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: The יצר הרע at first is like a thin spinning thread, and in the end it is like a cart rope.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers the question. Sin starts small and weak but grows into something very strong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two images in the פסוק show two stages of the יצר הרע. This fits מנשה, who began by mocking a few פסוקים and ended up in much worse sin.
steps.whatToRemember: Sin starts as a thin thread and grows into a thick rope. Small mockery can lead to great sin.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:
The evil inclination at first
is like a thin spinning thread,
and in the end it is like a cart rope.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי: יֵצֶר הָרָע בַּתְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cart rope is the יצר הרע after it has grown strong; it starts as a weak thread.

steps.title: Back to the פסוק: what is 'לוטן's sister was תמנע' teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to one of the פסוקים מנשה mocked and asks what it teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what we came to discuss, in any case: what is the point of 'לוטן's sister was תמנע'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the פסוק מנשה made fun of and asks what it really teaches. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בת קול said these פסוקים are not empty. Now the גמרא proves it by finding the lesson in one of them.

keyTerms.meaning: About what we came to discuss

phrases.english: About what we came to discuss, in any case,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to the פסוק מנשה mocked in step 12.

phrases.english: "Lotan's sister was Timna": what is its point?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי אסי's side point and returns to the פסוק from step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The lesson hidden in the פסוק about תמנע.

steps.title: תמנע was royalty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows from the title 'אלוף' that תמנע came from a royal family.
steps.simpleTranslation: תמנע was a daughter of kings, as it says 'the chief לוטן' and 'the chief תמנע,' and every chief is royalty without a crown.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer: תמנע was not an ordinary woman. She came from a family of rulers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both לוטן and תמנע are called 'אלוף', and an אלוף is a ruler without a crown. This detail matters for the story that comes next.

phrases.english: Timna was a daughter of kings,
as it is written: "The chief Lotan"
phrases.notes: בראשית 36:29

phrases.english: and "The chief Timna",
phrases.notes: בראשית 36:40

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל אַלּוּף – מַלְכוּתָא בְּלָא תָּאגָא הִיא.
phrases.english: and every chief is royalty without a crown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering step 17's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק shows that תמנע came from royalty.

steps.title: תמנע tried to convert and was turned away
steps.stepSummary: תמנע wanted to convert, but the אבות did not accept her. She chose to be a concubine in עשו's family, and עמלק came from her.
steps.simpleTranslation: She wanted to convert. She came to אברהם, יצחק and יעקב, and they did not accept her. She went and became a concubine to אליפז the son of עשו. She said: Better to be a maidservant to this nation than a noblewoman in another nation. From her came עמלק, who made ישראל suffer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story behind the פסוק. A princess gave up her status to be close to the family of אברהם, and עמלק came from her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we see why her royal status matters: she was willing to go from noblewoman to concubine just to attach herself to this family. Her son עמלק later became an enemy of ישראל.

phrases.english: She wanted to convert.
She came to Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov,
and they did not accept her.
She went and became a concubine
to Eliphaz the son of Esav.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה: מוּטָב תְּהֵא שִׁפְחָה לְאוּמָּה זוֹ
phrases.english: She said: Better that she be a maidservant to this nation
phrases.notes: She is talking about herself.

phrases.english: and not be a noblewoman in another nation.
From her came out Amalek,
who made Israel suffer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer by telling תמנע's story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תמנע was turned away from converting, attached herself to עשו's family, and gave birth to the line of עמלק.

steps.title: Why ישראל suffered from עמלק: they should not have pushed her away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that ישראל suffered from עמלק because the אבות should not have turned תמנע away.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because they should not have pushed her away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the lesson of the story. The suffering from עמלק came because a sincere woman who wanted to convert was rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the answer to step 17. The פסוק that מנשה called pointless actually teaches a serious lesson about pushing away someone who wants to come close. That proves the בת קול right: no פסוק in the Torah is empty.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'pointless' פסוק about תמנע teaches that the אבות should not have rejected her, and עמלק came as a result. Every פסוק in the Torah has meaning.
steps.whyThisMatters: It answers מנשה's mockery directly: a פסוק that looks like a family detail holds a lesson with consequences for all of Jewish history.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Meaning: why did ישראל deserve to suffer from עמלק?

phrases.english: Because they should not have pushed her away.
phrases.notes: "They" are the אבות who refused her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּלָא אִיבְּעִי לְהוּ לְרַחוֹקַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the story in step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק about תמנע teaches that rejecting her led to suffering from עמלק, which proves the Torah's details are not pointless.

steps.title: ראובן did not take wheat, only wild plants
steps.stepSummary: From ראובן going out at wheat harvest time and bringing home only דודאים, רב learns that צדיקים do not take what belongs to others.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And Reuven went in the days of the wheat harvest." רבא בר רבי יצחק said in the name of רב: From here we learn that the righteous do not stretch out their hands to steal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains another פסוק that מנשה mocked. It shows that even this simple-sounding story teaches a lesson about honesty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fields were full of wheat that belonged to other people. ראובן brought home only wild דודאים that belonged to no one. That shows a צדיק stays away even from small theft.
steps.whyThisMatters: It answers מנשה's mockery. A פסוק that looks like an unimportant detail actually teaches a moral lesson.

phrases.english: "And Reuven went in the days of the wheat harvest."
phrases.notes: בראשית 30:14. This is another one of the פסוקים מנשה made fun of.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא בְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rava son of Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rav said:
From here we learn about the righteous
that they do not stretch out their hands to theft.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן לְצַדִּיקִים שֶׁאֵין פּוֹשְׁטִין יְדֵיהֶן בְּגָזֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues going through the פסוקים מנשה mocked, after the תמנע discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדיקים avoid even small theft, as ראובן took only ownerless plants.

steps.title: What exactly are דודאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rest of the פסוק and asks what kind of plant דודאים are.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And he found דודאים in the field." What are דודאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a plain word question so we understand what ראובן found. It is setting up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing here is a challenge. The גמרא just wants to identify the plant named in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant ראובן found in the field

phrases.english: "And he found duda'im in the field."
What are duda'im?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same פסוק about ראובן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the plant called דודאים.

steps.title: Three opinions on what דודאים are
steps.stepSummary: רב, לוי, and רבי יונתן each name a different plant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: yavruchei. לוי said: violets. רבי יונתן said: seviskei.
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים answer the question, and each one names a different plant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a disagreement about identifying a plant, not about הלכה. The גמרא does not decide between them.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant, often understood as mandrakes

phrases.english: Rav said: yavruchei.
phrases.notes: A plant that many understand to be mandrakes.

phrases.english: Levi said: violets.
Rabbi Yonatan said: seviskei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three different plant names: yavruchei, violets, seviskei.
steps.whatToRemember: Every 'simple' פסוק that מנשה mocked has meaning: lessons in honesty, history, and even exact details like which plant ראובן found.

steps.title: Learning Torah for its own sake brings peace above and below
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלכסנדרי teaches that one who learns תורה לשמה brings peace to the heavenly group and the earthly group.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלכסנדרי said: Anyone who learns תורה for its own sake brings peace to the group above and the group below, as it says: "Or let him take hold of My strength; he will make peace for Me, peace he will make for Me."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: what real תורה learning accomplishes. רבי אלכסנדרי gives the first saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "My strength" is understood as the תורה. The word "peace" appears twice in the פסוק, which matches peace above (in heaven) and peace below (in this world).

keyTerms.meaning: Learning תורה for its own sake, not for honor or gain
The earthly group (people in this world)

phrases.english: Rabbi Alexandri said:
Anyone who learns Torah for its own sake
brings peace to the group above
and to the group below,
as it says: "Or let him take hold of My strength,

phrases.aramaic: יַעֲשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם לִי שָׁלוֹם יַעֲשֶׂה לִּי״.
phrases.english: he will make peace for Me, peace he will make for Me."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 27:5. "Peace" is said twice, one for above and one for below.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָעוֹסֵק בְּתוֹרָה לִשְׁמָהּ מֵשִׂים שָׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the פסוקים מנשה mocked to a new aggadic topic: the power of learning תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תורה לשמה brings peace in heaven and on earth.

steps.title: Torah learning is like building heaven and earth
steps.stepSummary: רב says one who learns תורה is like someone who built a palace above and below.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It is as if he built a palace above and below, as it says: "And I placed My words in your mouth, and in the shadow of My hand I covered you, to plant the heavens and set the foundations of the earth."
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a second description of what תורה learning does. It is as if the learner built heaven and earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links "My words in your mouth" (learning תורה) with planting the heavens and founding the earth. So the one who learns is described as a builder of both worlds.

phrases.english: Rav said: It is as if he built a palace
above and below,
as it says: "And I placed My words in your mouth,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 51:16.

phrases.english: and in the shadow of My hand I covered you,
to plant the heavens and set the foundations of the earth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second אמורא's description of the power of תורה learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning תורה is like building heaven and earth.

steps.title: Torah learning also protects the whole world
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds that the תורה learner protects the entire world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: He also protects the whole world, as it says: "And in the shadow of My hand I covered you."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן uses a different part of the same פסוק to add another benefit: the learner protects the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "also" shows he is adding to what came before. "The shadow of My hand" means protection, and the learner brings that protection to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: In the shadow of My hand

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף מֵגֵין עַל כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ,
phrases.english: He also protects the whole entire world,
as it says: "And in the shadow of My hand I covered you."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף מֵגֵין עַל כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק as רב to add another benefit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה learner protects the whole world.

steps.title: Torah learning also brings the redemption closer
steps.stepSummary: לוי adds that the תורה learner brings the גאולה closer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And לוי said: He also brings the redemption closer, as it says: "And to say to Zion, You are My people."
steps.whatsHappening: לוי uses the end of the same פסוק to add one more benefit: the learner speeds up the גאולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "You are My people" to ציון describes the time of redemption. Since it is in the same פסוק about "My words in your mouth," learning תורה helps bring it.

keyTerms.meaning: Zion, ירושלים and the Jewish people

steps.whatToRemember: One פסוק (ישעיהו 51:16) gives three benefits of תורה learning: building heaven and earth (רב), protecting the world (רבי יוחנן), and bringing the גאולה (לוי).

phrases.english: And Levi said:
He also brings the redemption closer,
as it says: "And to say to Zion, You are My people."
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק in ישעיהו 51:16.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third benefit from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תורה learning brings the גאולה closer.

steps.title: Teaching someone else's child is like making him
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says one who teaches תורה to another person's son is considered as if he made him.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Anyone who teaches תורה to his friend's son, the פסוק considers it as if he made him, as it says: "And the souls that they made in Haran."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from learning תורה to teaching it. ריש לקיש says the teacher is like the student's creator.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם and שרה did not actually create people in חרן. They taught them about השם, and the פסוק still calls it "making" them. So teaching counts as forming the student.

keyTerms.meaning: His friend's son, another person's child
The פסוק counts it for him

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמְלַמֵּד אֶת בֶּן חֲבֵירוֹ תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Anyone who teaches Torah to his friend's son,
the verse counts it for him as if he made him,
as it says: "And the souls that they made in Haran."
phrases.notes: בראשית 12:5. People can't create souls, so "made" here means they taught them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַמְלַמֵּד אֶת בֶּן חֲבֵירוֹ תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the benefits of learning תורה to the reward for teaching it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching another's child תורה is like having made that child.

steps.title: The teacher is as if he made the Torah itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the teacher is as if he made the words of תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: It is as if he made the words of תורה, as it says: "And you shall guard the words of this covenant and you shall make them."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a different view of what the teacher "made." It is not the student but the תורה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֹתָם" about the words of the covenant. רבי אלעזר reads "make them" in a strong way: by learning and teaching, you give the תורה's words a real existence.

keyTerms.meaning: The words of the covenant (the תורה)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
It is as if he made the words of Torah,
as it says: "And you shall guard the words of this covenant
and you shall make them."
phrases.notes: דברים 29:8. Usually read "do them," but here taken as "make them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different opinion about what the teacher is credited with making.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching תורה is like creating the words of תורה.

steps.title: The teacher is as if he made himself
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the same פסוק with different vowels: "make yourselves." The teacher builds himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is as if he made himself, as it says: "And you shall make them." Do not read "them" (אֹתָם) but "you" (אַתֶּם).
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third view on the same פסוק that רבי אלעזר used. Through an אל תקרי reading, he says the teacher shapes himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words אֹתָם and אַתֶּם have the same letters and differ only in vowels. Reading it as "you" teaches that the one who learns and teaches תורה is really building his own self.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read (a reading with different vowels to teach a lesson)

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not mean the פסוק is written wrong. The plain text stays the same; רבא uses a second way of reading the same letters to teach an extra lesson.
steps.whatToRemember: Teaching תורה makes three things: the student (ריש לקיש), the תורה itself (רבי אלעזר), and the teacher himself (רבא).

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is as if he made himself,
as it says: "And you shall make them" —
do not read "them" but "you."
phrases.notes: Same Hebrew letters, just different vowels, so "make them" becomes "make yourselves."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion, using the same פסוק as רבי אלעזר but read differently.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching and learning תורה shapes the teacher himself.

steps.title: Causing another to do a מצוה counts as doing it yourself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו teaches that one who causes a friend to do a מצוה is credited by the פסוק as if he did it himself, and quotes a פסוק as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו says: Anyone who gets his friend to do a מצוה, the verse treats him as if he did it himself. As it says: "and your staff, with which you struck the river."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a new rule: helping or getting someone else to do a מצוה earns you credit as if you did it. He then quotes a פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the earlier steps about the teacher being counted as if he "made" the student. Here the idea is wider: any time you bring about someone else's מצוה, it is credited to you. The proof from the פסוק is explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who causes his friend to do something
The פסוק credits him, or counts it for him
As if he did it himself

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמְעַשֶּׂה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ לִדְבַר מִצְוָה,
phrases.english: Anyone who causes his friend to do a מצוה,
the verse credits him as if he did it himself,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּמַטְּךָ אֲשֶׁר הִכִּיתָ בּוֹ אֶת הַיְאֹר״.
phrases.english: as it is said: "And your staff, with which you struck the river."
phrases.notes: שמות 17:5. ה׳ is speaking to משה here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: כׇּל הַמְעַשֶּׂה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ לִדְבַר מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of sayings about the great value of bringing others to תורה and מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who causes another to do a מצוה is credited as if he did it himself.

steps.title: How the staff verse proves the rule
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says משה struck the river, but אהרן actually struck it. So the פסוק must be teaching that the one who causes a מצוה gets credit for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did משה strike the river? Didn't אהרן strike it! Rather, it comes to tell you: anyone who gets his friend to do a מצוה, the verse treats him as if he did it himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the פסוק is a proof. It points out that אהרן struck the river, yet the פסוק says to משה "you struck."
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה told אהרן to strike the river, so משה caused the action. The פסוק still calls it משה's act. That shows that the one who causes an action is counted as if he did it.

keyTerms.meaning: But did...? A question that pushes back
Rather, it comes to tell you

phrases.english: But did Moshe strike it?
Didn't Aharon strike it!
Rather, it comes to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמְעַשֶּׂה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ לִדְבַר מִצְוָה,
phrases.english: Anyone who causes his friend to do a מצוה,
the verse credits him as if he did it himself.

steps.whatToRemember: The staff verse calls אהרן's strike משה's act, because משה caused it. If you cause a מצוה, it is credited to you.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֹשֶׁה הִכָּהוּ? וַהֲלֹא אַהֲרֹן הִכָּהוּ!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in step 31 supports רבי אבהו's rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one who causes a מצוה is credited as its doer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 17:5 calls the striking of the river משה's act, even though אהרן did it (שמות 7:19–20).

steps.title: Two views on who counts as an אפיקורוס
steps.stepSummary: Back to the משנה's list: רב and רבי חנינא say an אפיקורוס is one who disgraces a תלמיד חכם. רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי say it is one who disgraces another person in front of a תלמיד חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: אפיקורוס: רב and רבי חנינא both say this is someone who disgraces a תלמיד חכם. רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי say this is someone who disgraces his friend in front of a תלמיד חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's word אפיקורוס and brings two views on what kind of person it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views link אפיקורוס to disrespect connected with a תלמיד חכם. The first view needs the scholar himself to be disgraced. The second view says even disgracing someone else in a scholar's presence is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the people the משנה says has no share in עולם הבא
One who disgraces or treats with contempt

phrases.english: Epikoros:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is returning to a word from the משנה's list of people with no share in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Rav and Rabbi Chanina both say,
this is one who disgraces a Torah scholar.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמְרִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַמְבַזֶּה חֲבֵירוֹ בִּפְנֵי תַּלְמִיד חָכָם.
phrases.english: this is one who disgraces his friend in front of a Torah scholar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶפִּיקוֹרוֹס: רַב וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by defining a term from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two definitions of אפיקורוס: disgracing a תלמיד חכם, or disgracing another person in front of a תלמיד חכם.

steps.title: What is left for the phrase מגלה פנים בתורה?
steps.stepSummary: The second view has room left for the phrase מגלה פנים בתורה, since disgracing the scholar himself fits there. But under the first view, disgracing a scholar is already called אפיקורוס, so what does מגלה פנים בתורה mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says that disgracing your friend in front of a תלמיד חכם is an אפיקורוס: disgracing the תלמיד חכם himself would be מגלה פנים בתורה שלא כהלכה. But for the one who says that disgracing the תלמיד חכם himself is an אפיקורוס, what would מגלה פנים בתורה be?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the first view. If disgracing a תלמיד חכם is already the אפיקורוס, then what kind of person is the separate category מגלה פנים בתורה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate categories, אפיקורוס and מגלה פנים בתורה, and each needs its own meaning. The second view easily gives each category a different act: disgracing someone in front of a scholar for one, and disgracing the scholar himself for the other. The first view has already used up the act of disgracing a scholar, so it needs a different case for מגלה פנים בתורה.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense according to... A setup before a difficulty
According to the one who says
One who "reveals faces in the Torah": treats or explains the תורה in a wrong, disrespectful way

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack that disproves the first view. It is a question asking that view to give the phrase מגלה פנים בתורה its own meaning, and the next step answers it.

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who says:

phrases.aramaic: הַמְבַזֶּה חֲבֵירוֹ בִּפְנֵי תַּלְמִיד חָכָם אֶפִּיקוֹרוֹס הָוֵי,
phrases.english: one who disgraces his friend in front of a Torah scholar is an epikoros,
then one who disgraces the Torah scholar himself

phrases.aramaic: מְגַלֶּה פָּנִים בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא כַּהֲלָכָה הָוֵי.
phrases.english: is one who reveals faces in the Torah not according to halacha.
But according to the one who says:

phrases.aramaic: מְבַזֶּה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם עַצְמוֹ אֶפִּיקוֹרוֹס הָוֵי,
phrases.english: one who disgraces the Torah scholar himself is an epikoros,
one who reveals faces in the Torah would be like what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first view from step 33 against the separate category מגלה פנים בתורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Under the view of רב and רבי חנינא, what case is meant by מגלה פנים בתורה?

steps.title: Example: מנשה בן חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: Under the first view, מגלה פנים בתורה means someone like מנשה בן חזקיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like מנשה בן חזקיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with an example. מגלה פנים בתורה means a person like the king מנשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנשה mocked the stories and verses of the תורה. That is a different wrong from disgracing a scholar. So the first view can give each category its own meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: Menashe, the king who was the son of King Chizkiyahu

phrases.english: Like Menashe son of Chizkiyah.

steps.whatToRemember: Under רב and רבי חנינא's view, אפיקורוס means disgracing a scholar, and מגלה פנים בתורה means mocking the תורה itself, like מנשה did.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מגלה פנים בתורה refers to someone like מנשה, who mocked the תורה's verses.

steps.title: Another version: the dispute is about מגלה פנים בתורה
steps.stepSummary: Some teach that the same argument between רב and רבי חנינא and between רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי was about the phrase מגלה פנים בתורה, not about אפיקורוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some teach it on the later clause: מגלה פנים בתורה. רב and רבי חנינא say: this is one who disgraces a תלמיד חכם. רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי say: this is one who disgraces his friend in front of a תלמיד חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the argument. In this version, the same two opinions define מגלה פנים בתורה instead of אפיקורוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opinions are worded the same way, but they now explain a different term. Since the argument is now about מגלה פנים בתורה, the question from step 34 falls away. The next step raises the mirror-image question instead: under one view, what is left for אפיקורוס?

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (in another way)

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it on the later clause:
"One who reveals faces in the Torah."
Rav and Rabbi Chanina say:
This is one who disgraces a Torah scholar.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַמְבַזֶּה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ בִּפְנֵי תַּלְמִיד חָכָם.
phrases.english: This is one who disgraces his friend in front of a Torah scholar.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions. In one, the argument defines אפיקורוס. In the other, the same argument defines מגלה פנים בתורה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of where the step 33 argument belongs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the second version, מגלה פנים בתורה means either disgracing a תלמיד חכם, or disgracing another person in front of one.

steps.title: Under the second view, who is the אפיקורוס?
steps.stepSummary: The first view has a clear place for both phrases. Under the second view, the case of disgracing a friend before a scholar is already used up for מגלה פנים בתורה, so what is an אפיקורוס?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says that disgracing a תלמיד חכם himself is מגלה פנים בתורה, because then disgracing a friend in front of a תלמיד חכם is an אפיקורוס. But the one who says that disgracing a friend in front of a תלמיד חכם is מגלה פנים בתורה: who is the אפיקורוס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking a question about the second version of the argument. Under one view, both cases have a place. Under the other view, the גמרא wants to know who the אפיקורוס is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two bad behaviors and two labels. The first view uses the bigger one, disgracing the scholar himself, for מגלה פנים בתורה. It then uses the smaller one, disgracing a friend in front of him, for אפיקורוס. The second view uses the smaller behavior for מגלה פנים בתורה, and disgracing the scholar himself is surely at least as bad, so the label אפיקורוס now needs a new case.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for one side); this sets up a contrast with the side that has a problem
One who 'shows a face' against the Torah: treats the Torah with disrespect
A person who scorns Torah scholars and Torah authority
Like whom? Asking for an example case

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who says
that one who disgraces a Torah scholar himself
is one who shows disrespect to the Torah,
and one who disgraces his friend in front of a Torah scholar
is an אפיקורוס.
But according to the one who says
that one who disgraces his friend in front of a Torah scholar
is one who shows disrespect to the Torah,
an אפיקורוס is like whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the second version of the argument given in step 36
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Under the view that disgracing a friend before a scholar is מגלה פנים בתורה, what case is an אפיקורוס?

steps.title: רב יוסף: one who says the scholars only help themselves
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that an אפיקורוס is someone who says the רבנן do nothing for us, because they learn only for their own sake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: like those who say, 'What good have the רבנן done for us? They read Torah for themselves and they learn for themselves.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives an example of an אפיקורוס under the second view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person does not insult any specific scholar in front of him. He looks down on the whole idea that Torah learning helps anyone except the learner. That kind of scorn for Torah scholars as a group is his case of אפיקורוס.

keyTerms.meaning: What good have the רבנן done for us?

phrases.english: רב יוסף said:
Like those who say:
What good have the Rabbis done for us?
They read for themselves, they learn for themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כְּגוֹן הָנֵי דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 37
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An אפיקורוס is one who claims the רבנן's learning benefits only themselves

steps.title: אביי: that person denies the Torah itself
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that someone who says the scholars don't help the world is denying a פסוק. That makes him a מגלה פנים בתורה, not just an אפיקורוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: this person is also a מגלה פנים בתורה, as it is written: 'If not for My covenant day and night, I would not have set the laws of heaven and earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's answer. The case he gave belongs under מגלה פנים בתורה, so it can't be the example of אפיקורוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches that the world exists because of the Torah, which is learned day and night. So learning Torah does help everyone. Someone who says it doesn't help is contradicting the Torah itself, and that is the heavier label, מגלה פנים בתורה.

keyTerms.meaning: My covenant (here understood as the Torah)
The laws of heaven and earth: the order of nature

phrases.english: אביי said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מְגַלֶּה פָּנִים בַּתּוֹרָה נָמֵי הוּא,
phrases.english: This one is also one who shows disrespect to the Torah,
as it is written:
"If not for My covenant day and night,
I would not have set the laws of heaven and earth."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 33:25. The world stays standing because of Torah learned day and night, so the scholars do help everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הַאי מְגַלֶּה פָּנִים בַּתּוֹרָה נָמֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's example of an אפיקורוס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying the scholars don't benefit the world contradicts a פסוק, so it is מגלה פנים בתורה. That label is already taken in this view, so it can't be the example of אפיקורוס.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: another פסוק showing the righteous protect a place
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק backs up אביי's point with the פסוק about sparing a whole place because of its righteous people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: you can learn it from here too, as it says, 'I will spare the whole place for their sake.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a second source for אביי's idea that righteous people and Torah scholars protect everyone around them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that a whole city can be saved because of the righteous people in it. So the scholars clearly benefit others. This makes it even stronger that denying their benefit means denying the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will spare (literally, I will carry or forgive)

phrases.english: רב נחמן בר יצחק said:
From here too you can learn it,
as it is said:
"Then I will spare the whole place for their sake."
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:26. ה׳ tells אברהם He would save סדום if there were righteous people in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source supporting אביי's objection
steps.raayaObject: The idea that righteous people and scholars benefit those around them
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 18:26, about sparing סדום for the sake of the righteous

steps.title: New answer: a student who doesn't honor his teacher when quoting
steps.stepSummary: Since רב יוסף's case was rejected, a new example of אפיקורוס is given: a student who repeats a teaching in front of his רבי in a way that doesn't show him honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like someone sitting in front of his רבי. A teaching he learned somewhere else comes to his mind, and he says, 'This is what we say there,' instead of saying, 'This is what the master said.'
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רב יוסף's case, the גמרא gives a new example of an אפיקורוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a small, quiet lack of respect: the student treats his teacher like an equal instead of giving him credit. It is lighter than disgracing a friend in front of a scholar. So it fits the lighter label, אפיקורוס, under the second view.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what the master said: a respectful way of quoting

phrases.english: Rather, like one who sits in front of his teacher,
and a teaching from another place comes to his mind,
and he says: "This is what we say there,"
and he does not say: "This is what the master said."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's rejected answer with a new example
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An אפיקורוס is a student who quotes a teaching before his teacher without honoring him as the source

steps.title: רבא: like the house of בנימין the doctor
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives another example of an אפיקורוס: people like the family of בנימין the doctor, who ask what good the רבנן have ever done for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: like those of the house of בנימין the doctor, who say: 'What good have the רבנן done for us? Never…'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers his own example of an אפיקורוס. Their words continue in the next part of the גמרא, so this sentence is not finished here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first this sounds like רב יוסף's rejected case, because these people also ask what the רבנן have done for them. The word מעולם ("never") begins their complaint, and the rest of it comes in the next lines. That rest will show how their complaint is different from what רב יוסף described.

keyTerms.meaning: The house (family) of בנימין the doctor

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop here thinking רבא simply repeated רב יוסף's rejected answer. The sentence starting with מעולם continues in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.english: רבא said:
Like those of the house of בנימין the doctor,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרִי: מַאי אַהֲנוֹ לַן רַבָּנַן מֵעוֹלָם?
phrases.english: who say: "What good have the Rabbis done for us? Never…"
phrases.notes: The word מעולם starts the next part of their complaint, which continues in the next lines of the גמרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן הָנֵי דְּבֵי בִּנְיָמִין אָסְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question of step 37
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An אפיקורוס is like the people of the house of בנימין the doctor, who complain that the רבנן never did anything for them (their words continue in the next part)
